new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (the PDF's metadata gives the Title 'OPD', Author 'SIL PNG Branch', created 2004-09-20, 5 pp., text present). extracted text p.4 reads exactly: 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) / Primary stress is on the first syllable. Compound words take additional secondary stress on the additional component.' -- verbatim as quoted (only a layout line-wrap inside 'additional component'). Surrounding p.4 material is diphthong inventory above and 'Syllable Patterns' (V, VC, VCC, CV, CVC, CCV, CVCC, CCVC with syllabified examples) below; nothing else on stress, no tone or length contrast claimed, no stress-marked examples; bibliography cites Shim, Jae Wook 1993 OPD ms. Reading fixed: initial s…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the first syllable of the word; in compounds each additional member carries a secondary stress (on its own first syllable, by implication). No tone or length contrast is reported under the suprasegmentals heading.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Only in compounds: 'Compound words take additional secondary stress on the additional component.' Nothing said about rhythmic secondary stress in long simplex words.
new_statements.exceptions: None in the OPD. Consistent incidental remarks in Dondorp & Shim (2013[1997]) p.28: peripheral case markers are 'unstressed monosyllabic particles which cliticize to the NP', and p.72 postpositions may be 'destressed and turn into clitics'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement in a short SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet (no acoustic evidence, no examples with stress marks). Variety: northern (Wipim) dialect, the basis of SIL work (Dondorp & Shim p.7). Note Josefsson (2025:47) states Wipi prosody is 'entirely undescribed', having apparently not used the OPD's suprasegmental line; Wurm (1975) claims at stock level a 'complex stress system with rhythm principles' plus a low-load two-tone system for Eastern Trans-Fly generally, which the Wipi OPD does not echo.
new_statements.identity_note: The SIL materials (OPD and Grammar Essentials) describe the northern dialect as spoken in Wipim (also Podare, Yamega); Dondorp & Shim p.7 distinguish a northern and a southern (Oriomo River / Dorogori / Ume / Kuru) dialect with 67-84% cognacy between them. Language names Gidra, Jibu, Oriomo all = glottocode wipi1242, ISO gdr.

sources.citation: Josefsson, Michael W. (2025). Deep-time diversity: The Oriomo languages of Southern New Guinea. MA thesis, Australian National University. ix+101 pp.
sources.note: p.47: 'Our knowledge of Oriomo prosody is vanishingly small: there is word-initial stress in Bine (Döhler, in press: 6), but for Wipi and Gizrra prosody is entirely undescribed.' (overlooks the OPD one-liner; lists Wipi linguistic sources as Dondorp & Shim 1997 and Shim mss. 1993, 2000a, 2000b only).

sources.citation: Wurm, Stephen A. (1975). The Trans-Fly (sub-phylum-level) stock. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1, 323-344. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Stock-level generalisation only (sec. 2.6.1.6): Trans-Fly languages 'all share a suprasegmental system which manifests itself in a complex stress system with rhythm principles', and Kiwaian and Eastern Trans-Fly families 'seem to possess a two-tone system with usually low to very low functional load'. Nothing specific to Gidra/Wipi.

sources.citation: Dondorp, Anne and Jae-Wook Shim (2013 [1997]). Wipi Grammar Essentials. Written Jan 1997; formatted for online publishing by Ruth Wester, Nov 2013. Ukarumpa: SIL-PNG. 128 pp.
sources.note: Ch.2 'Phonological description' (pp.10-13) covers orthography, phoneme charts and morphophonemics only, defers phonology to the OPD (Shim & Shim 1993); no stress rule. Only incidental: p.28 'The peripheral case markings are phonologically bound, unstressed monosyllabic particles which cliticize to the NP'; p.72 postpositions 'destressed and turn into clitics'.
